answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, any supplier switch (memory_c2) carries onboarding and integration risk that could interrupt scheduled deliveries—unacceptable given the objective to avoid increasing delivery risk. Deferring (memory_c5) isn't viable since this is the critical primary contract, not a non-critical one, and it lapses in 14 days. Adding a second source (memory_c3) addresses resilience but not the mandated 18% cost cut, and can't be stood up in 14 days for a primary role. Renegotiating with the incumbent (memory_c4), reinforced by the pattern in memory_c6 where multi-year commitments unlocked volume pricing without narrowing scope, offers a path to real cost reduction while preserving the stability seen in memory_c1—no migration work, no delivery interruption, fits the 14-day window. I verified memory_c4 and memory_c2 to confirm the negotiated-margin outcome was genuine and to size the vendor-switch savings as a comparison baseline before ruling it out for this cycle. This defers the vendor-switch and second-sourcing questions to the next review cycle, which is an acceptable tradeoff given only one decision slot is available now.
